expected_segments: These are original study checklists. Use the cited lessons for the detailed rules and limitations; a tick does not certify a vehicle or driver as safe.
Establish that the driver is legally permitted and actually fit to drive. Resolve uncertainty about fatigue, medication or conditions before leaving. See M01-L01/L02.
Check the route, weather, traffic, realistic timing, stopping opportunities and a fallback option. Include the return journey. See M01-L04 and M07-L04.
Check the vehicle, usable visibility, required lighting and controls. Confirm protection for each passenger. See M02.
Establish load and trailer limits, coupling and securing if relevant. Verify the vehicle's recorded status and obligations. See M08.
Prepare navigation and passenger help before moving. Keep attention available for traffic. See M07-L03.
Observe: What can I see, what is hidden and who might enter?
Identify the duty: Which rule, sign, marking, signal or authorised instruction applies?
Preserve space: Can I stop or alter the plan without forcing another person to avoid me?
Communicate: Will others understand my intended movement?
Recheck: Is the information still true as I begin and complete the action?
This is an original learning routine based on the observation, risk and cooperation aims of the category B syllabus. It is not an official test sequence.

Check that stopping and parking are permitted at that location, time and for that vehicle. Meet fee, duration and permit conditions. Secure against rolling and unauthorised use. Check for people before opening doors and provide a safe place for passengers to leave. See M05-L03/L04 and the Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§47–55.
Use the official Transportstyrelsen catalogue alongside this illustrated reference. Study the exact sign, panel and context—not only a simplified shape mnemonic.

Road-sign illustrations: Transportstyrelsen. Source links and verification dates are recorded in the official references. Swedish names are official. English names and explanations are editorial translations. Examples are independent, not verified sign assemblies.

For each item, explain the action in your own words, identify one plausible misunderstanding and practise it in a changed situation. The sign descriptions and their legal meanings are in the Road Signs Regulation. A printed still image alone cannot demonstrate flashing, changing, audible or hand-movement signals; learn the sequence as well as the appearance.
Identify the hazard and choose an earlier observation or speed response.
State whether to stop or yield and identify the conflicting traffic.
Determine the restricted action, vehicle, weight, dimension or speed and its extent.
Choose the required path or recognise a road/area regime and its end.
Identify the destination and mode, choose a lane early and avoid a late turn.
Locate a destination while still checking access rules.
Read the actual message and the road-user or facility symbol.
Combine the main sign with time, distance, length, direction or vehicle qualifications.
Distinguish lane boundaries, warnings, crossing locations and stopping/parking instructions.
Identify which traffic is controlled and what the current indication requires.
Recognise an authorised direction and respond to it.
Read changed road alignment, closures and railway warnings.

These are plain-language learning explanations, not a certified legal translation. Legal meanings remain in the linked official provisions and the lessons that use them.
Learner permit required for the ordinary learning route.
Practise driving under the applicable requirements.
Duty to yield, clearly and in time.
Duty to make a complete stop at the prescribed position.
The general yielding rule for a vehicle approaching from the right.
Priority road, with its associated rules.
Road shoulder, with its own use restrictions.
Distinct cycle passage / cycle crossing arrangements.
Roundabout traffic arrangement / its central island.
Cycle street with special vehicle duties.
Motorway / expressway subject to access and movement restrictions.
Level crossing between road and rail/tram on its own track formation.
Winter road conditions, including snow, ice, slush or frost.
Defined ready weight / registered maximum weight.
Registered for road use / formally placed off road.
Environmental zone with specified vehicle criteria.
Vision Zero: no one killed or seriously injured in road traffic.
A brief involuntary sleep episode; do not treat alertness tricks as a cure.
Temporary spare wheel, used only within the actual vehicle handbook limits.
Electrical fuse protecting its circuit from excessive current.
Vehicle structure designed to deform and manage crash energy.
Front-grip loss can widen the turn; rear-grip loss can make the rear step outward.
Water separates tyre contact from the road, reducing grip/control.
Downward load at the trailer coupling, distinct from whole trailer weight.
Lorry with registered total weight at most 3,500 kg.
Automatic driving prohibition after a missed inspection deadline; restricted trips apply.
CO impairs blood oxygen transport; added fossil CO₂ contributes to warming.
NOx: airway irritation, acidification and ground-level ozone formation.
In a conventional manual car, slowing with accelerator released and suitable gear engaged.
Plug-in hybrid externally rechargeable; conventional non-plug-in hybrid is not.
Coolant / cooling-system cap; a hot pressurised system can release scalding liquid or steam.
Repeat this entry after study or supervised practice. Its purpose is honest self-assessment, not a score predicting an examination result.

A useful entry identifies something observable. “Check the near cycle path before the turn, then revisit it as the gap develops” is more actionable than “be better at junctions.” Keep adapting the task to your own experience and the feedback from your instructor or supervisor.
